chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Bandaneeji told us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ziyad ibn Marwan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

The Cry is inevitable, the Sufyani is inevitable, the Yamani is inevitable, and the killing of the pure soul is inevitable, and a hand appearing from the sky is inevitable. (He said): And a fright in the month of Ramadan will awaken the sleeper, terrify the awake, and bring the girl out of her veil.

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيُّ: Al-Sufyani (a specific leader/sign of the end times)
key_terms.النَّفْسُ الزَّكِيَّةُ: The pure soul (referring to a specific martyrdom figure)
key_terms.النِّدَاءُ: The Cry (a celestial sound signaling the end times)
key_terms.الْيَمَانِيُّ: Al-Yamani (a specific leader/sign of the end times)

ai.seo_question: What are the inevitable signs preceding the appearance of the Mahdi according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* emphasizes the inevitability (*min al-mahmum*) of major eschatological signs, framing the Sufyani, Yamani, and the killing of the Pure Soul (*Nafs al-Zakiyya*) as fixed events in Shia cosmology. The mention of a 'fright' (*fuz'a*) in Ramadan highlights the spiritual turbulence preceding the Mahdi's appearance, linking cosmic signs with temporal religious events. This narrative underscores the transition from the era of occultation to the era of appearance, a central theme in Twelver Shia exegesis.
